abstract: Young-onset dementia (YOD) disrupts the family system during a critical stage of life. Families affected by YOD often navigate child-rearing, work/community obligations, and caring for aging parents in the context of progressive cognitive decline in a middle-aged partner or parent. We explore four domains that define the lived experience of YOD: (1) financial strain, (2) safety challenges, (3) social isolation, and (4) systemic deficiencies within the healthcare and workplace infrastructure.
title: The distinct challenges of living with young-onset dementia.
